requirement: The controlled JavaScript target must perform a real zstd level-3 encode and decode in JavaScript, without calling WebAssembly, a native process, or a host compression intrinsic; the result must interoperate with an independent zstd 1.5.7 decoder before the workload can claim implementation coverage.

candidates.name: fzstd
evidence: The published API exports decompression and streaming decompression only.
Its README identifies the package as pure-JavaScript Zstandard decompression; it cannot execute the catalog-required encode step.

candidates.name: zstdify
evidence: On a deterministic 32 KiB binary probe, zstdify level 3 compressed and self-decompressed successfully, but the independent zstd 1.5.7 CLI rejected the emitted frame with exit 1 and 'Data corruption detected'.
On a deterministic 1 MiB valid JSON probe, zstdify level 3 threw 'FSE readNCount: truncated input' during compression and produced no frame.
A codec that self-roundtrips a frame rejected by the reference implementation is not a trustworthy controlled encoder for the frozen workload.

candidates.name: @foxglove/wasm-zstd and equivalent browser packages
evidence: These packages expose the official C codec compiled to WebAssembly.
Using one for the JavaScript target would make both variants Wasm and violate the controlled target contract.

candidates.name: zstd.ts and native Node bindings
evidence: The package shells out to system-installed zstd and unzstd programs.
A native subprocess is neither browser-runnable JavaScript nor equivalent to the declared controlled pair.

nextAction: Keep the workload at 0 coverage. Re-evaluate only when a pinned, license-compatible pure-JavaScript zstd encoder and decoder passes official zstd vectors, all 1/10/100 MiB registered fixtures, independent zstd 1.5.7 interoperability, and the controlled algorithm/fixed-level review.
